diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate} be satisfied.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated under Assumption 1 only, but the bound contains E||Dξ||^2, requiring ξ∈D^{1,2}, and the |π| term relies on Theorem main convergence rate, which requires Assumption main assumption convergence rate (ξ∈D^{2,q}, f∈C^{1:2}, etc.). The proof also uses Lemma lem:malliavin-energy, which assumes f∈C^{1:1}. Thus the result is not valid as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypotheses (e.g., Assumption main assumption convergence rate for the |π| term, ξ∈D^{1,2} for the Malliavin term, and f∈C^{1:1} for the energy estimates) to Theorems thm:added-4 and thm:added-5, or explicitly restrict their statements to those regimes.
issues.overall_effect: The main convergence guarantees for the exact and Monte Carlo chaos-Euler schemes are not established under the stated assumptions; they only hold under additional unstated Malliavin and regularity conditions, narrowing the advertised scope of general L^2 terminal conditions.
issues.title: Main error estimates stated under insufficient assumptions
issues.why_classification: The main convergence theorems are invalid as stated. Repairing requires adding significant assumptions that exclude general square-integrable terminal conditions and require Malliavin regularity, which is a major loss of advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 only gives ξ∈L^2. The quantity V_m(ξ) involves E[ξ^2 H_a^2], which requires ξ∈L^4 to be finite in general. A square-integrable random variable need not have a fourth moment, so the claim is false.

failure_location.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by assuming ξ∈L^4 or directly assuming V_m(ξ)<∞ for the Monte Carlo rate.
issues.overall_effect: The finiteness of V_m(ξ) and hence the meaningfulness of the Monte Carlo error bound in Theorem thm:added-5 for general L^2 terminal conditions is not guaranteed.
issues.title: False claim that Assumption 1 implies fourth moments for ξ
issues.why_classification: The false remark affects the applicability of the Monte Carlo convergence rate but can be fixed by adding a moment condition or assuming V_m finite. It narrows the scope but does not invalidate the core exact chaos result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $a = (a_1, \dots, a_M)$, let us define $\widetilde{h}_{a} = \sqrt{n!}/\sqrt{a!} \ h_{1}^{\otimes a_{1}} \widetilde{\otimes} \cdots \widetilde{\otimes} h_{M}^{\otimes a_{M}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The family \tilde h_a is built from a fixed finite set h_1,...,h_M. It spans only the symmetric tensor products of the span of these M functions, which is a proper subspace of \tilde L^2(T_n) when M is finite. It is not a basis of the whole space.

failure_location.quote: One can easily check that $(\widetilde{h}_{a})_{|a| = n}$ forms an orthonormal basis of $\widetilde{L}^{2}(\mathcal{T}_{n})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the statement to say it forms an orthonormal basis of the subspace spanned by the symmetrized tensor products of h_1,...,h_M.
issues.overall_effect: This incorrect statement could mislead about the completeness of the truncated basis; however, the subsequent error bounds correctly treat it as a projection onto a subspace, so the main results are not invalidated by this alone.
issues.title: False claim that truncated Hermite family is an orthonormal basis of the full symmetric space
issues.why_classification: It is a local false statement not used crucially, and the correction is straightforward without affecting any substantive claim.
